Subject: Budget range validation — monthly spend band & procurement thresholds

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the candid feedback on inference latency and the integration questions. As promised, sharing a quick follow-up to confirm the budget band and procurement thresholds so we can size the right Dedicated capacity and draft the SOW.

High level asks from our side:
- Confirm expected monthly token volume (approx.) for PoC and for production (tokens/month).
- Confirm procurement sign-off threshold (PO limit needing VP/Finance sign-off).
- Any target unit economics you’re aiming for (e.g., $/1M tokens target).

Initial notes based on our conversation and the usage profile you described:
- PoC (1–3 months): 50–200M tokens/month — estimated monthly spend band $4k–$16k depending on model (+ egress).
- Production ramp: 500M–5B tokens/month — typical spend bands we see: $40k–$400k/month.
- Target $/1M tokens: crosswalk attached in redwood_pricing_options.xlsx with ballpark unit costs for open models, Redwood-verified variants, and reserved capacity discounts.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_options.xlsx (price bands + example unit economics), sample MA & procurement notes.

Next steps: if you can reply with the two items above (monthly token estimate + procurement threshold), I’ll route this to Marissa to confirm technical fit and to Dylan for any commercial exceptions/discount authority. We can then draft a mutual action plan (MAP) and circulate an initial SOW.

Best,

Laura, thanks for the follow-up and for the spreadsheet — helpful. Quick answers from our side:

- Expected tokens: PoC ~150M tokens/month (internal chatbots + one retrieval pipeline). Production (12mo target) ~1.2B tokens/month if adoption goes well.
- Procurement threshold: at our org a PO under $100k can be approved by our Procurement Manager; anything over $100k requires VP Finance approval and a 30-day review.
- Target unit economics: we’re trying to keep total infra + API cost under $35k/month at 1.2B tokens — ballpark target ~ $29–30 / 1M tokens (including basic caching). Happy to adjust if your numbers say otherwise.

We’ll attach our internal procurement thresholds doc (see skyline_procurement_thresholds.pdf). Can you confirm what discounts / reserved capacity pricing you'd anticipate at 1B+ tokens? Also need an estimated timeline for onboarding Dedicated vs Hosted API for a regulated workload.

Thanks — Alex

Subject: Re: Budget range validation — monthly spend band & procurement thresholds

Alex — great, thanks for the clarity. Based on your numbers I put together a simple unit-economics summary (also in the attached spreadsheet):

Summary (ballpark estimates):
- PoC (150M tokens/mo): Hosted API plan (on-demand) estimated cost: $8k–$12k/month depending on model choice and caching.
- Production (1.2B tokens/mo): Reserved / Dedicated pricing estimates:
  - Conservative reserved profile (no committed discount): ~$120k–$150k/month (hosted + burst).
  - Committed Dedicated profile (12mo commit + 20% discount): ~$96k–$120k/month.
  - Aggressive enterprise discount (25–35%): could bring it to ~$78k–$90k/month with a multi-year commit and larger token commitments.

Equivalent $/1M tokens (approx):
- Hosted PoC: $53–$80 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated conservative: $100–$125 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated committed (20%): $80–$100 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive enterprise: $65–$75 / 1M tokens

Notes and assumptions:
- These include inference costs + basic caching. They do not include optional add-ons (longer retention for traces, premium SLAs, on-prem packaging).
- We can optimize unit economics with quantized model variants and KV-prefix caching (Marissa can run a quick eval on your typical prompts to give a tighter cost estimate).
- Procurement threshold of $100k means VP Finance sign-off will be required for the more conservative Dedicated profile. We often structure a PoC (hosted) phase followed by a committed Dedicated conversion to reduce approval friction.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you run the prompt eval on Skyline sample prompts and give a 2-tier estimate (standard vs quantized model) by EOD Monday?
- Dylan: given the $100k procurement threshold, can you confirm discount approval levels we can offer in a 12mo commit?
- Alex / Procurement: we’ll draft an MAP and a draft SOW once Marissa’s numbers are in.

Attaching: redwood_pricing_options.xlsx (detailed bands).

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Alex / Procurement team — looping in Dylan and confirming next steps from the commercial/ops side.

Quick notes:
- Procurement threshold of $100k is clear; for anything >$100k we’ll need VP Finance sign-off from Skyline. We typically handle that with a short MAP + SOW and a PO template.
- Based on Laura’s breakdown and your 1.2B token target, I recommend a staged approach:
  1) PoC on Hosted API for 6–8 weeks (150M tokens/month) to validate latency + prompts — estimated spend $8k–$12k.
  2) Commit to a 12mo Dedicated profile after successful PoC with an initial 6mo ramp clause. This structure often shortens procurement review since the initial monthly invoice can be kept under the $100k threshold while the commitment gives you price protection.

Dylan — can you weigh in on discount authority? Laura and I propose a 20% list discount for a 12mo commit at the 1.2B/mo profile, with a path to an additional 10% (30% total) for a larger multi-year agreement. If that’s acceptable I’ll prepare the MAP + initial SOW and send a DocuSign link for signatures along with a PO template.

Alex — I’ll also add a short appendix to the MAP that lists the assumptions we used for the $/1M token calculations and the steps to switch from Hosted to Dedicated with minimal downtime.

Next steps for Procurement: please confirm whether a 30-day review window for >$100k is acceptable and whether Skyline requires any vendor-specific terms in the MA (I’ve attached a redline-ready MA draft — ma_draft_v3.pdf).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
